chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Hanan ibn Sadeer from Abi Salam al-Abdi who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: What do you say about a man who deliberately delays the Asr prayer? He said: He will come on the Day of Judgment deprived of his family and wealth. I said: May I be your ransom, and even if he is from the people of Paradise? He said: And even if he is from the people of Paradise. I said: And what is his status in Paradise? He said: Deprived of his family and wealth, he will be a guest among its people; he will not have a house of his own in it.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who deliberately delays Asr prayer in Paradise?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explaining that deliberate delay of Asr prayer results in being 'mawtur' (deprived) of one's family and wealth, a state that persists even for those destined for Paradise. This unique punishment signifies a loss of spiritual presence and status, rendering the individual a transient guest rather than a permanent resident in Jannah. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the temporal quality of worship, where neglecting the specific time of Asr diminishes one's standing in the hereafter despite ultimate salvation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Hanan b. Sadeer from Abi Salam al-’Abdi who said:

“Yes, even if he is worthy of Paradise, he will be brought without relatives and wealth on the Day of Judgment.” The narrator asked, “What position will he get in Paradise?” Imam answered, “He will be deprived of relatives and wealth over there also. Such a person will have no house and he will have to stay as a guest in others’ houses in Paradise.”
